messages:
incident-bot: ALERT triggered: high tail latency on /v1/generate (p95 > 3s) in us-east-1. Pager duty: paged oncall.

Alex G: oncall here, seeing spike across multiple nodes in us-east-1. Rolling 5m avg p95 at ~4.8s, errors still low but timeouts creeping.

Priya S: thanks — are we seeing CPU/GPU saturation or network? any host-level anomalies?

Alex G: quick checks: GPU util normal, CPU normal. network rx/tx for affected hosts shows elevated retransmits on eni-eni pairs. attaching short log:
```
node-12: netstat -s | grep retransmit
TCP retransmit: 1723
node-15: TCP retransmit: 1689
```

Manu K: @Alex G can you switch routing to fallback pool (non-us-east) for critical traffic? wont fully fix but reduces customer impact.

Alex G: initiating gradual routing fallback now (policy: 20% -> 50% -> 100%), will monitor.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-347 created, priority P1. Escalation to SRE leads.

James R: I'm on vendor contact. Opening escalation with AWS NOC (premium). Furnishing p95 graphs, host lists, and retransmit counters.

James R: message sent to AWS Support with ticket #CASE-888102. Contacted via phone and included packet captures.

AWS Support: Thanks for the report. We've engaged the network team and are investigating an elevated packet loss signature in us-east-1 affecting ENI paths. We will update within 15 minutes.

Priya S: good. drafting a status page update — pulling concise wording below for review: 

```
STATUS (draft): We are investigating increased request latency for text generation in US-East. Some requests may experience higher than normal latency (2–10s). Our engineers are working with the cloud provider. Mitigation: partial routing fallback to alternate region and temporary model-size fallback for affected customers. No evidence of data loss. Updates every 15 minutes.
```

Alex G: LGTM. Add note about impacted region and recommended workaround for customers (retry/backoff).

customer-ops: Suggest adding escalation contact for enterprise customers and note that Dedicated customers are isolated (if true). Also include how to get live updates (status.redwood.ai/incidents).

Manu K: also drafting short customer notification for affected customers (email/console banner):

```
Customer notification (draft): We are currently investigating increased latency affecting text generation in the US-East region. You may see longer response times or transient delays. Our mitigation includes routing traffic to alternate region and reduced model size for latency-sensitive paths. If you need immediate assistance, please contact support@redwood.ai or reply to this message. We will provide updates as we have them.
```

Priya S: good. I'll post the status page draft after we confirm fallback fully active at 50% and AWS acknowledgement. Alex, what's the current fallback percentage?

Alex G: fallback at 50% now. p95 for fallthrough requests dropped from 4.8s -> 1.2s. overall cluster p95 still ~2.1s.

James R: AWS NOC responded: they see an ECMP flapping pattern in a subset of ToR switches affecting ENI traffic in a single AZ. They are performing microcode swap and targeted path reconvergence. ETA initial mitigation ~18 minutes.

Leah M: I'll take first-hand handoff in 20m when Alex heads out for other pager tasks. Alex, drop a short summary for incoming oncall and the playbook steps you ran.

Alex G: handoff summary:
- Issue: elevated TCP retransmits causing p95 latency in us-east-1 (likely cloud network).
- Actions taken: paged vendor, initiated routing fallback (50%), enabled model-size fallback for latency-critical API route, posted draft status.
- Relevant artifacts: packet captures attached to CASE-888102, netstat counts, metric dashboard link (internal).
- Next steps for Leah: coordinate with AWS updates, confirm when ENI retransmits drop to baseline, ramp fallback down to 0 after cloud fix, send final customer update.

Leah M: got it. I'll monitor AWS updates and hold on to the case. tagging @AWS Support for real-time updates.

AWS Support: Update: microcode swap completed in affected ToR switches. Network team reports ECMP reconverged; monitoring shows retransmits returning to normal. Please validate on your side and advise when you can start ramping fallback down.

Alex G: validating... running checks:
```
for node in node-12 node-15 node-18; do netstat -s | grep retransmit; done
# outputs now show retransmit counts near baseline
```

Alex G: retransmits down to expected levels. p95 back to ~0.9s for majority, overall p95 1.1s. starting rollback of routing fallback to 20% -> 0 over 5m.

Priya S: once rollback complete, let's finalize status page and customer notification with resolved language. Draft resolution note: 

```
RESOLVED: Root cause: transient network ECMP flap in AWS us-east-1 ToR switches causing elevated TCP retransmits and increased request latency. Mitigation: microcode swap and reconvergence by AWS network team; Redwood applied temporary region routing and model-size fallback. Impact: increased request latency (2–10s) for some users in US-East. No data loss. Actions taken: routing fallback, model fallback, vendor escalation. Timeline: incident opened at ${thread_start_time}, resolved at ${thread_end_time}. For follow-ups, contact support@redwood.ai.
```

customer-ops: approve. Add note offering post-incident call for any enterprise customers who experienced impact.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-347 status changed to RESOLVED.

Alex G: closing out — Leah please create postmortem doc with timeline and follow-up action to improve detection (we should add ENI retransmit alerting) and vendor SLA checklist. thanks everyone.

Leah M: on it, will create doc and ping the infra team for ENI alerting.

AWS Support: Closing the case from our side as network path normalized. If you observe further anomalies, reopen or contact us directly.

Leah M: final note posted to status page and customer-notify sent. incident closed.
